user_questions.question: 1) Who is the 'account owner' to notify on suspension: (a) owner of the related Account, Storefront__c.Account__r.Owner (recommended; Account__c is set on all 21 storefronts), or (b) the Storefront record owner, Storefront__c.OwnerId? 2) Notification channel: (a) email (recommended), (b) in-app custom notification (needs a new CustomNotificationType), or (c) both? 3) 'Start as Pending Activation': (a) picklist default plus a validation rule that blocks creating a storefront in any other status (recommended), or (b) picklist default only?
user_questions.simulated_answer: All four rules as stated: notify the account owner (the related Account's owner). For channel and insert enforcement: No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: Step 5 says to ask the scope question 'as soon as a fork is known, before I when discovery already shows it'; I found the recipient fork (Account__r.Owner vs OwnerId) during verification but sent I with the recipient pre-tagged as 'user decision' before asking. The skill has no explicit checkpoint between step 3 and step 4 forcing the scope message first; a hard 'send the scope message before I if any fork is open' gate would prevent this.

AskCoworker repeatedly tagged facts I supplied as '[Verified: prior session]' and re-injected components from its own earlier proposal (Account_Owner_Email__c, EmailTemplate) into R even though the accepted inventory had dropped them, plus an unrelated Onboarding_Application__c item in T. The response-handling table covers 'unrelated content' but not 'echoes of rejected inventory rows'.
AskCoworker picklist formulas used = / != instead of ISPICKVAL; rule 'Wrong details in proposals' covered it, but a hint in the I template to use valid formula syntax could reduce corrections.

R and T resend rule: I split the single flow into two flows after R and T were sent (inventory row changed 13 -> 14). Step 5 says to resend R and T if a scope decision changes the inventory after them, but is silent when the change is a self-correction under Rule 3/step 4; I did not resend and relied on my own analysis.
